Oxygen and ventilatory support.recommendation: Oxygen is recommended in patients with SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg to correct hypoxaemia.
Intubation is recommended for progressive respiratory failure persisting in spite of oxygen administration or non-invasive ventilation.

Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation should be considered in patients with respiratory distress (respiratory rate >25 breaths/min, SpO2 <90%) and started as soon as possible to decrease respiratory distress and reduce the rate of mechanical endotracheal intubation.

Diuretics.recommendation: Intravenous loop diuretics are recommended for all patients with AHF admitted with signs/symptoms of fluid overload to improve symptoms.
Combination of a loop diuretic with thiazide-type diuretic should be considered in patients with resistant oedema who do not respond to an increase in loop diuretic doses.

Vasodilators.recommendation: In patients with AHF and SBP >110 mmHg, i.v. vasodilators may be considered as initial therapy to improve symptoms and reduce congestion.
